draft.title: Presenting findings
card: Presenting findings means communicating the results of an investigation so that others can follow and check them. Each method suits a different kind of information.
Maps and graphs
A map shows where something happens, such as where flood damage was worst. A graph shows numbers, such as a line graph of rainfall over a year, so patterns and changes can be seen.
Photographs
A photograph shows what a place looked like on the day. It should be labelled with the location and what it shows, so it supports a point in the report.
Written report
A clear report links the pieces together. It answers the original question, uses the evidence from the maps, graphs and photographs, and states a conclusion.
draft.remember: Choose the method that best shows the evidence, then use it to answer the question.

a.q: Which presentation method is best for showing where litter was found along a beach?
opts: A map marking each site where litter was found
A line graph of the litter collected each week
A photograph with no label or location
A conclusion with no supporting evidence
a.why: A map shows where things are, so it suits a question about location. A line graph shows change in numbers over time, which is a different job and does not show where the litter was.

b.q: Priya measured daily temperatures in a park for a month and wants to show how they changed. She also wants to explain what her results mean. Which plan fits best?
opts: A line graph of temperatures, then a written report
A map of the park only, with no report
Photographs only, with no labels or numbers
A written report only, with no graph or evidence
b.why: A line graph shows how numbers change over time, and a written report explains the results and answers the question. A map alone shows location, not change in temperature across a month, so it does not fit Priya's data.
b.clue: Match the method to numbers over time, then to explaining.

a.best: A map marking each site where litter was found

b.best: A line graph of temperatures, then a written report

problems.detail: The right option is the only one without 'only' or 'no ...'. Every distractor is visibly crippled ('Photographs only, with no labels', 'A map of the park only, with no report', 'A written report only, with no graph or evidence'), so a student can pick the answer without knowing which method suits numbers over time.
Two distractors are obviously defective ('with no label or location', 'with no supporting evidence'), leaving only the line graph as a real alternative. That makes the question very easy for Year 11.

check.summary: The facts and intended answers are correct. Question b gives itself away because every wrong option is marked 'only'/'no', and question a's distractors are too obviously wrong for Year 11.

proposal.title: Presenting findings
card: Presenting findings means communicating the results of an investigation so that others can follow and check them. Each method suits a different kind of information.
Maps and graphs
A map shows where something happens, such as where flood damage was worst. A graph shows numbers, such as a line graph of rainfall over a year, so patterns and changes can be seen.
Photographs
A photograph shows what a place looked like on the day. It should be labelled with the location and what it shows, so it supports a point in the report.
Written report
A clear report links the pieces together. It explains what the results mean, uses the evidence from the maps, graphs and photographs, and states a conclusion that answers the question.
proposal.remember: Choose the method that best shows the evidence, then use it to answer the question.

a.q: Which presentation method is best for showing where litter was found along a beach?
opts: A map marking each site where litter was found
A line graph of the litter collected each week
A labelled photograph of litter at the busiest site
A pie graph of the types of litter collected
a.why: A map shows where things are, so it suits a question about location along the beach. A labelled photograph is tempting, but it shows what one site looked like, not where litter was found across the whole beach.
a.clue: The question asks about where, across the whole beach.

b.q: Priya measured daily temperatures in a park for a month and wants to show how they changed. She also wants to explain what her results mean. Which plan fits best?
opts: A line graph of temperatures, then a written report
A map of the park, then a written report
Labelled photographs of the park, then a written report
A line graph of temperatures, then labelled photographs
b.why: A line graph shows how numbers change over time, and a written report explains the results and states a conclusion. The graph with photographs is tempting, but photographs only support a point, so nothing in that plan explains what the results mean.
b.clue: One method must show numbers over time, the other must explain.
